thesis: As intelligence becomes abundant and inference unit prices compress, provider-to-provider token price comparison may lose strategic relevance. Measure the incremental cost and product value of adding StegGate governance to an existing model service.
primary_comparison_unit: incremental cost per governed admissible outcome
secondary_comparison_units: governance premium as percent of underlying inference cost
incremental latency per governed admissible outcome
incremental bytes and receipt-storage cost per governed admissible outcome
admissibility lift relative to raw model execution
provider gross-margin headroom for a governed AI product tier
required_inputs: raw and governed normalized outcome hash

abundant_intelligence_modes.condition: underlying inference cost remains a material fraction of governed product cost
underlying inference cost approaches commodity pricing and no longer dominates total product value
abundant_intelligence_modes.primary_metric: absolute incremental governance cost per admissible outcome

abundant_intelligence_modes.condition: model outputs are sufficiently substitutable that provider intelligence price is no longer the main differentiator
abundant_intelligence_modes.primary_metric: cost and reliability of converting an ungoverned model output into an authorized, admissible, reconstructable execution

product_hypothesis.name: Governed AI
product_hypothesis.provider_offer: Existing model service plus StegGate execution governance, admissibility decisioning, receipts, reconstructability, and policy enforcement.
product_hypothesis.commercial_question: What incremental wholesale cost must a provider add to its current AI product to offer a governed tier, and what retail price preserves target margin?
non_claims: StegVerse makes the underlying model more intelligent
all providers should charge the same governed premium

claim_boundary: This schema measures incremental governance cost and productization economics around a bounded admissible execution outcome. It does not establish universal provider economics, enterprise ROI, model superiority, or market willingness to pay.
